{"id": "2d14353e-b8ee-4abe-9553-dff4a421ab2f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good — this confirms the likely culprits. Since regular chat works but Q Apps 403s even with clean IAM/Identity Center assignment, the gap is almost always one of these three things, in order of likelihood:

**1. Subscription tier — most common cause**
Q Apps is a **Pro-only** feature. If the user is on **Amazon Q Business Lite** ($3/user), they'll get chat working fine but a 403 on anything Q Apps related, since Lite doesn't include Q Apps at all. Check their subscription tier assignment in the Q Business console (tiers are assigned per-user, separate from Identity Center group assignment).

**2. Q Apps not enabled at the application level**
Even for Pro users, Q Apps must be explicitly turned on as a feature setting on the Q Business application itself ("admin controls and guardrails"). If the application admin never enabled the Q Apps capability, every user — regardless of tier — gets a 403 trying to open it.

**3. Missing `qapps:*` IAM actions on the web experience role**
Q Apps uses its own IAM namespace (`qapps:...` actions like `CreateQApp`, `CopyQApp`, `CreateLibraryItemReview`, etc.) distinct from `qbusiness:...` actions. Regular chat only needs `qbusiness:Chat`/`qbusiness:ListConversations`-type permissions. If the web experience IAM role grants `qbusiness:*` but was never updated with the `qapps:*` statements (notably true for roles created before July 10, 2024, when Q Apps permissions were restructured), chat works but Q Apps throws 403. Also worth checking: did the account's Q Apps **service-linked role** get created? It's auto-created when `QAppsConfiguration` is enabled — if it's missing or was manually removed, Q Apps calls fail even with an otherwise-correct role.

**Suggested diagnostic order:**
1. Confirm the user's subscription tier is **Pro**, not Lite, in the Q Business console.
2. Confirm Q Apps is toggled **on** in the application's feature/admin settings.
3. Diff the web experience IAM role against the current Q Apps IAM policy sample (`qbusiness:ListIndices`, `qbusiness:ListDataSources`, plus the `qapps:*` actions) — look specifically for a role that predates the July 2024 Q Apps permission update.
4. Verify the Q Apps service-linked role exists in the account.

Want me to pull the actual Q Business application config and the web experience IAM role from this account to check these directly?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
